    url.match? BASECAMP_CAMPFIRE_WEBHOOK_URL_REGEX
  end

  def for_campfire?
    url.match? CAMPFIRE_WEBHOOK_URL_REGEX
  end

  def for_slack?
    url.match? SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL_REGEX
  end

      Rails.application.config.action_mailer.default_url_options ||

    options[:http_host] = [ url_options[:host], url_options[:port] ].compact.join(":") if url_options[:host].present?

require "net/http"
require "openssl"
require "resolv"

class Webhook::Delivery < ApplicationRecord
  USER_AGENT = "fizzy/1.0.0 Webhook"
  STALE_THRESHOLD = 7.days

  OPEN_TIMEOUT = 7
  READ_TIMEOUT = 7
  WRITE_TIMEOUT = 5

  HTTP_ERRORS = [
    EOFError,
    IOError,
    Net::HTTPBadResponse,
    Net::HTTPHeaderSyntaxError,
    Net::OpenTimeout,
    Net::ProtocolError,
    Net::ReadTimeout,
    Net::WriteTimeout,
    OpenSSL::SSL::SSLError,
    Resolv::ResolvError,
    SocketError,
    SystemCallError,
    Timeout::Error,
    URI::InvalidURIError
  ].freeze

  belongs_to :account, default: -> { webhook.account }
  belongs_to :webhook
  belongs_to :event

  store :request, coder: JSON
  store :response, coder: JSON

  enum :state, %w[ pending in_progress completed errored ].index_by(&:itself), default: :pending

  scope :ordered, -> { order created_at: :desc, id: :desc }
  scope :stale, -> { where(created_at: ..STALE_THRESHOLD.ago) }

  class << self
    def cleanup
      stale.in_batches.delete_all
    end
  end

  def deliver_later
    Webhook::DeliveryJob.perform_later(self)
  end

  def deliver
    return unless deliverable? && claim_for_delivery

    perform_delivery
    record_delivery_outcome
  end

  def sanitized_request
    if headers = request&.dig("headers")&.except("X-Webhook-Signature")
      { headers: headers }
    end
  end

  def response_summary
    if response.present?
      { code: response[:code], error: response[:error] }
    end
  end

  def failed?
    (errored? || completed?) && !succeeded?
  end

  def succeeded?
    completed? && response[:error].blank? && response[:code].between?(200, 299)
  end

  private
    def deliverable?
      pending? && webhook.active? && Webhook.where(id: webhook_id, active: true).exists?
    end

    def claim_for_delivery
      if self.class.where(id: id, state: :pending).update_all(state: :in_progress, updated_at: Time.current) == 1
        reload
        true
      else
        false
      end
    end

    def perform_delivery
      uri = URI.parse(webhook.url)
      payload = render_payload
      headers = request_headers(payload)

      self.request = { headers: headers }

      if ip = resolve_public_ip(uri)
        http_response = send_request(uri, ip, payload, headers)
        self.response = { code: http_response.code.to_i }
        self.state = :completed
      else
        self.response = { error: :destination_unreachable }
        self.state = :errored
      end

      save!
    rescue *HTTP_ERRORS
      self.response = { error: :destination_unreachable }
      self.state = :errored
      save!
    end

    def render_payload
      Current.with(account: account, user: nil) do
        if webhook.for_basecamp?
          { content: render_event(formats: :html).strip }.to_json
        elsif webhook.for_campfire?
          render_event(formats: :html).strip
        elsif webhook.for_slack?
          { text: render_slack_text }.to_json
        else
          render_event(formats: :json)
        end
      end
    end

    def render_event(formats:)
      webhook.renderer.render(
        template: "webhooks/event",
        formats: formats,
        layout: false,
        assigns: { event: event }
      )
    end

    def render_slack_text
      fragment = Nokogiri::HTML.fragment(render_event(formats: :html))
      fragment.children.map do |node|
        if node.name == "a"
          "<#{node["href"]}|#{node.text}>"
        else
          node.text.gsub("&", "&").gsub("<", "<").gsub(">", ">")
        end
      end.join.squish
    end

    def request_headers(payload)
      {
        "User-Agent" => USER_AGENT,
        "Content-Type" => content_type,
        "X-Webhook-Signature" => signature(payload),
        "X-Webhook-Timestamp" => event.created_at.utc.iso8601
      }
    end

    def content_type
      if webhook.for_campfire?
        "text/html"
      else
        "application/json"
      end
    end

    def signature(payload)
      OpenSSL::HMAC.hexdigest("SHA256", webhook.signing_secret, payload)
    end

    def resolve_public_ip(uri)
      return nil unless Webhook::PERMITTED_SCHEMES.include?(uri.scheme)
      return nil if uri.hostname.blank?

      if ip = parse_ip(uri.hostname)
        ip.to_s unless SsrfProtection.blocked_address?(ip)
      else
        SsrfProtection.resolve_public_ip(uri.hostname)
      end
    end

    def parse_ip(hostname)
      IPAddr.new(hostname)
    rescue IPAddr::InvalidAddressError
      nil
    end

    def send_request(uri, ip, payload, headers)
      http = Net::HTTP.new(uri.hostname, uri.port)
      http.ipaddr = ip
      http.use_ssl = uri.scheme == "https"
      http.open_timeout = OPEN_TIMEOUT
      http.read_timeout = READ_TIMEOUT
      http.write_timeout = WRITE_TIMEOUT

      http_request = Net::HTTP::Post.new(uri.request_uri, headers)
      http_request.body = payload

      http.request(http_request)
    end

    def record_delivery_outcome
      delinquency_tracker = webhook.delinquency_tracker || webhook.create_delinquency_tracker!
      delinquency_tracker.record_delivery_of(self)
    end
end
EOF

**My Thoughts on the Webhook Delivery Process**

Okay, this is beautifully orchestrated. It's so clean, from event to delivery! When an event kicks off on a board, it's immediately linked to `Event::RelayJob` via `after_create_commit`. That job then grabs the event and finds all the active webhooks for that event's board that are subscribed to the event's action, and triggers the webhooks.

Triggering a webhook is where the magic really begins. We atomically verify its active state, that it's subscribed to the event, and that a delivery doesn't already exist for this event, all under a lock. This ensures exact-once delivery! It then creates a pending `Webhook::Delivery` and enqueues `Webhook::DeliveryJob` on the `:webhooks` queue.

The job itself is well-defined. First, a check of deliverability: it makes sure it's pending, that the webhook is still active, and that the webhook still exists and is active. Then, an atomic claim of the delivery to prevent duplicates, which is crucial. After that, it renders the payload. The rendering uses Jbuilder, with specific payloads for Basecamp, Campfire, and Slack, which is very thoughtful. Everything is handled within `Current.with` for a clean context.

Headers are meticulously constructed, including a `X-Webhook-Signature` for integrity using HMAC-SHA256, and `X-Webhook-Timestamp`. SSRF protection is built-in with public IP resolution using `SsrfProtection`. HTTP POST is handled with specific timeouts and no redirects.

We carefully log the request and response, including the `code` and any errors, and update the delivery state. The `delinquency_tracker` then takes over. If the delivery succeeded, we reset any failure counters. If it failed, we increment the failure count and track the first failure time. This is key: if we hit 10 consecutive failures within an hour, the webhook gets automatically deactivated! That's a great safeguard.

The admin can manually reactivate the webhook, which resets the failure tracking. Finally, a scheduled cleanup job removes deliveries older than 7 days, which is excellent for keeping things tidy.

The delivery log is readily accessible, providing details on state, request, response, and event. The delivery logs are also rendered in HTML in the recent deliveries view, offering a convenient way to inspect the state of each delivery.

require "test_helper"

class Webhook::DelinquencyTrackerTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  setup do
    @webhook = webhooks(:active)
    @tracker = @webhook.delinquency_tracker
  end

  test "single failure records first_failure_at and increments count" do
    freeze_time

    @tracker.record_delivery_of(failed_delivery)

    @tracker.reload
    assert_equal 1, @tracker.consecutive_failures_count
    assert_equal Time.current, @tracker.first_failure_at
    assert @webhook.reload.active?
  end

  test "ten consecutive failures over an hour deactivates the webhook" do
    freeze_time
    first_failure_time = Time.current

    9.times do
      @tracker.record_delivery_of(failed_delivery)
      travel 7.minutes
    end

    assert_equal 9, @tracker.reload.consecutive_failures_count
    assert_equal first_failure_time, @tracker.first_failure_at
    assert @webhook.reload.active?

    @tracker.record_delivery_of(failed_delivery)

    assert_equal 10, @tracker.reload.consecutive_failures_count
    assert_equal first_failure_time, @tracker.first_failure_at
    assert_not @webhook.reload.active?
  end

  test "ten consecutive failures within less than an hour keeps the webhook active until an hour passes" do
    freeze_time

    10.times do
      @tracker.record_delivery_of(failed_delivery)
      travel 5.minutes
    end

    assert_equal 10, @tracker.reload.consecutive_failures_count
    assert @webhook.reload.active?, "should stay active before an hour has elapsed"

    travel 10.minutes # total elapsed: 60 minutes since first failure
    @tracker.record_delivery_of(failed_delivery)

    assert_equal 11, @tracker.reload.consecutive_failures_count
    assert_not @webhook.reload.active?
  end

  test "fewer than ten failures over more than an hour keeps the webhook active" do
    freeze_time

    @tracker.record_delivery_of(failed_delivery)
    travel 2.hours

    8.times do
      @tracker.record_delivery_of(failed_delivery)
    end

    assert_equal 9, @tracker.reload.consecutive_failures_count
    assert @webhook.reload.active?
  end

  test "a successful delivery resets the failure streak" do
    freeze_time

    9.times do
      @tracker.record_delivery_of(failed_delivery)
      travel 10.minutes
    end

    assert_equal 9, @tracker.reload.consecutive_failures_count

    @tracker.record_delivery_of(succeeded_delivery)

    @tracker.reload
    assert_equal 0, @tracker.consecutive_failures_count
    assert_nil @tracker.first_failure_at
    assert @webhook.reload.active?

    @tracker.record_delivery_of(failed_delivery)
    assert_equal 1, @tracker.reload.consecutive_failures_count
    assert @webhook.reload.active?
  end

  test "errored deliveries count as failures" do
    freeze_time

    @tracker.record_delivery_of(errored_delivery)
    travel 1.hour

    8.times { @tracker.record_delivery_of(errored_delivery) }
    assert @webhook.reload.active?

    @tracker.record_delivery_of(errored_delivery)
    assert_not @webhook.reload.active?
  end

  test "reactivating a deactivated webhook resets tracker so a single failure does not switch it off again" do
    freeze_time

    @tracker.record_delivery_of(failed_delivery)
    travel 1.hour
    9.times { @tracker.record_delivery_of(failed_delivery) }

    assert_not @webhook.reload.active?

    @webhook.activate
    assert @webhook.reload.active?
    assert_equal 0, @tracker.reload.consecutive_failures_count
    assert_nil @tracker.first_failure_at

    @tracker.record_delivery_of(failed_delivery)
    assert @webhook.reload.active?
    assert_equal 1, @tracker.reload.consecutive_failures_count
  end

  private
    def failed_delivery
      Webhook::Delivery.new(webhook: @webhook, event: events(:layout_commented), state: :completed, response: { code: 500 })
    end

    def errored_delivery
      Webhook::Delivery.new(webhook: @webhook, event: events(:layout_commented), state: :errored, response: { error: "destination_unreachable" })
    end

    def succeeded_delivery
      Webhook::Delivery.new(webhook: @webhook, event: events(:layout_commented), state: :completed, response: { code: 200 })
    end
end

class Webhook::DelinquencyTracker < ApplicationRecord
  DELINQUENCY_THRESHOLD = 10
  DELINQUENCY_DURATION = 1.hour

  belongs_to :account, default: -> { webhook.account }
  belongs_to :webhook, inverse_of: :delinquency_tracker

  def record_delivery_of(delivery)
    if delivery.succeeded?
      reset
    elsif delivery.failed?
      record_failure
    end
  end

  def reset
    with_lock do
      update!(consecutive_failures_count: 0, first_failure_at: nil)
    end
  end

  private
    def record_failure
      target_webhook = webhook

      with_lock do
        self.first_failure_at ||= Time.current
        self.consecutive_failures_count = consecutive_failures_count.to_i + 1
        save!
        target_webhook.deactivate if delinquent?
      end
    end

    def delinquent?
      consecutive_failures_count >= DELINQUENCY_THRESHOLD && failing_for_too_long?
    end

    def failing_for_too_long?
      first_failure_at.present? && first_failure_at <= DELINQUENCY_DURATION.ago
    end
end
